- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (positive sentiment > 0.5) — model tends to overshoot, especially after spikes.
- Underestimate prices in bearish sentiment (negative or low sentiment < 0.3) — model is too conservative, often missing sharp reversals.
- Lag in price correction: model delays downward adjustments after strong upward moves, especially when sentiment dips.
- Mean reversion bias: model overcorrects after sharp spikes, leading to overprediction in early days of a correction.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts are overly optimistic in early periods (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is volatile — adjust downward by 1–2% for high sentiment.
- Overshoot after sentiment reversal: if sentiment drops sharply, model continues to forecast upward — reduce forecast by 3–5% for 3–5 days post-reversal.
- Ignore sentiment when price is flat or near support — model tends to overreact to minor fluctuations in low-volatility periods.
